articles.title: Mike Tomlin is a Super Bowl-winning coach. His real passion might have been ‘Minecraft.’
articles.summary: As the coach of one of the NFL’s most successful franchises, the Pittsburgh Steelers, for nearly two decades, Mike Tomlin was charged with building championship-caliber teams.
articles.body: As the coach of one of the NFL’s most successful franchises, the Pittsburgh Steelers, for nearly two decades, Mike Tomlin was charged with building championship-caliber teams. In his free time, Tomlin was building something different: an elaborate cityscape in the video game “Minecraft.” On his YouTube channel on Wednesday, Tomlin revealed part of that map, which he said he had been working on for more than 12 years. Within four hours, the episode had been viewed more than 334,000 times. By the next morning, that total had doubled. “I’ve always had an interest in architecture and so forth,” Tomlin said in the video, which has amassed over 900,000 views. “And so I started building this creative city.” Tomlin may have been perfecting the map for more than a decade, but his hobby had only become public three weeks earlier. The 54-year-old stepped down as the Steelers’ coach in January after 19 consecutive winning seasons, which included a Super Bowl victory. As his debut season as a broadcaster for NBC’s “Sunday Night Football” began last month, Tomlin revealed in an interview with Craig Melvin that his passions, in fact, ranged beyond football. Watching his then-young children spend hours playing “Minecraft” had inspired him to see what all the fuss was about. As they became teenagers and went off to college, their interest waned. Not Tomlin’s, though. “More than anything, it was therapeutic for me,” Tomlin said. “So, mindless entertainment. I’m not a big TV watcher. It allowed me to detach from the realities and the pressures of life.” With the Steelers, Tomlin was known for unique sayings referred to as “Tomlinisms.” In 2020, he famously wouldn’t allow Covid restrictions to be used as a hardship, saying, “We do not care.” So it stunned some football fans last month to hear that what Tomlin privately did care so much for was a video game that is immensely popular with elementary-age kids. Since its creation in 2009, “Minecraft” has become the bestselling game of all time, with more than 300 million copies sold, Microsoft said in 2024, and has since spawned a popular movie. An open-world “sandbox” game, “Minecraft” allows users to build whatever their creativity desires using a variety of materials, from different types of stone and wood to beyond. Some players build fantasy worlds where building physics don’t apply. Players often build in multiple maps. Tomlin stuck to just one, however, preferring to build what appears to be a midsize city centered around bodies of water and with a dense urban core that includes sports stadiums, high-rises and a PNC Bank. The map showed hills and wooded suburbs. In other words, not all that dissimilar to … Pittsburgh. Narrating his tour with a matter-of-fact delivery not out of place from his past weekly news conferences, Tomlin used verbiage a real estate developer would approve of while saying that his map all began by creating a bay. Then he built a boutique hotel, complete with an executive spa, therapy rooms and an “appropriate number of public restrooms.” Showing off a glass ceiling over the hotel’s conference room, Tomlin called his design philosophy “lighting-conscious.” Some commenters online questioned how much time Tomlin had spent building while also working in the NFL, an industry known for its workaholic culture. Former Steelers running back Le’Veon Bell wrote, “we were tryna win super bowls and coach T was on minecraft building cities 😭.” More so, the reaction tended to center on Tomlin’s dedication to realism. “Never thought I’d watch Mike Tomlin discuss lighting and basement speakeasies,” one YouTube commenter said. On a Reddit thread devoted to Tomlin’s build, one person wrote, “When Mike Tomlin first mentioned this whole thing, I was NOT expecting such an impressive city!” Tomlin built buildings by themes, intentionally placing them next to rivers, bays and lakes he carved out of the map. His designs are intricate; residential buildings included different floor plans for the penthouse than the lower floors. Kitchens featured islands. Bathrooms featured plants. Bedrooms included paintings. The living spaces in one high-rise, which was down the street from buildings named “CVS” and “7-Eleven,” wrapped around a central aquarium. Nearby were stadiums for professional soccer and baseball. At some point, Tomlin acknowledged becoming “obsessed with rooftop penthouses” with great views. That focus then spilled over into designing spaces for indoor and outdoor entertainment, balconies, home offices, and his-and-hers bathroom concepts. “Find someone who loves you like Coach Tomlin loves a Jack & Jill bathroom,” another YouTube commenter said. It was one of many jokes sparked by Tomlin’s “Minecraft” devotion. Yet, perhaps it shouldn’t have been all that surprising. In “Minecraft,” Tomlin seems to have found similarities to the mixture of creativity and discipline required in the world of the NFL. Coaches’ lives abide by a rigid structure of practices, games and the offseason calendar. They conceive exotic play designs and defensive coverages, then put them into practice by obsessing over details and precision. “Football is an emotional game played by high-energy men who are really emotional,” Tomlin said in 2022. “They need to hear a steady voice. They need to hear consistency in messaging in belief, and so it’s my job to exemplify that.” Tomlin was praised as a coach for his never-too-high, never-too-low personality. The kind of person whose idea of winding down after a long day in the spotlight might include ensuring his “Minecraft” map had a “certain density,” as he said. When Tomlin dropped his son Dino off at college, he said he was inspired to re-create the look of off-campus housing into his own city. “Bro I used to come home sometimes and my PlayStation would just be gone,” one of Tomlin’s sons, Mason, posted on X. “And I wasn’t in trouble.” At one point during Tomlin’s tour, he focused on a tall, beige building labeled “Trump Tower.” “Not an endorsement,” a chyron said on the video. “This build is (circa) 2015… We didn’t think he would win. Twice.” Its penthouse had an “unbelievable open floor plan,” Tomlin said approvingly. He promised his roughly 76,000 YouTube subscribers more episodes. “I’ll give you a tour of this aquarium at some point,” he said. “It’s crazy.”

articles.title: In 1998, a wide receiver the NFL had blacklisted in the draft fell to the 21st pick; 1 season later, he had rewritten every receiving record a rookie had ever touched and the league was quietly terrified
articles.summary: Randy Moss waited. Twenty teams passed on the Marshall receiver in the 1998 NFL draft, most of them worried about his past, not his hands.
articles.body: Randy Moss waited. Twenty teams passed on the Marshall receiver in the 1998 NFL draft, most of them worried about his past, not his hands. Minnesota took him at No. 21. Within months he was a problem defenses could not solve. Moss caught 69 passes for 1,313 yards and 17 touchdowns, a rookie record for touchdown catches that still stands. He made the Pro Bowl, won Offensive Rookie of the Year, and helped a 15-1 team. The sharpest part of the story is not the slide. It is how little the league understood what it was ignoring.Why Randy Moss fell to No. 21 in the 1998 NFL DraftTalent was never the question. Moss had scored more than 50 touchdowns in two seasons at Marshall, and every scout knew it. The question was his record away from the field. As a teenager in West Virginia he was convicted of battery after a fight at his high school, spent time in jail and lost a scholarship offer from Notre Dame. Florida State signed him, then dismissed him after a positive marijuana test violated his probation. Marshall gave him a third start.Draft rooms are cautious places. A receiver who runs like Moss but carries that file makes general managers nervous, and they remember the picks that blow up. Some teams reportedly took him off their boards entirely. So he sat while the names kept coming. Twenty were called before his, including Ryan Leaf, Andre Wadsworth and Curtis Enis, none of whom came close to his career.Why Minnesota Vikings took the riskThe Vikings were not a desperate team. They had gone 9-7 the year before, with Dennis Green running the sideline and Cris Carter owning one side of the field. Randall Cunningham took over at quarterback early that season. Carter had his own rough chapter, released by Philadelphia in 1990 over substance problems, and he knew what a second chance felt like. Moss would not have to carry the offense or be the loudest voice in the room.It was a smart fit more than a gamble. Defenses already had to worry about Carter, which meant Moss often saw single coverage. Put a deep threat in that spot and the math changes fast.What Randy Moss actually did as a rookieHe started fast and never really slowed. His 69 catches went for 1,313 yards, an average of 19.0 per grab. His 17 touchdowns led the league and remain the most ever by a rookie. Minnesota finished 15-1 and scored 556 points, the most in NFL history at that point.Part of the damage came from how he played. Moss had long, gliding strides that made corners think they were fine until the ball was already in the air. He tracked deep throws better than most receivers with twice his experience, and he caught contested balls like they were gifts.His loudest day came on Thanksgiving in Dallas, a team that had passed on him. He caught three touchdowns, finished with 163 yards and the Vikings won. Cowboys fans got a close look at what they had skipped.The season ended badly. Atlanta beat Minnesota in overtime in the NFC title game after Gary Anderson, perfect on field goals all year, missed a late kick. Moss deserved a Super Bowl shot that year and never got one.Did Randy Moss really rewrite every rookie record?Not quite, and it is worth correcting because the real story holds up on its own. The touchdown mark still stands. The yardage mark did not last. Anquan Boldin, Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase have all passed 1,313 yards as rookies, and Chase reached 1,455 in 2021. Moss no longer sits near the top of that list.As for the league being terrified, regret is closer to the truth. Teams had every chance to take him and chose not to. After his first season, they could not unsee what they had missed. Defensive coordinators spent the next decade building coverage plans around him, and few found a reliable answer.What the Randy Moss slide still teaches scoutsHis fall is now a standard case study in how teams weigh character against production. The cost of passing is easy to measure in hindsight. Moss retired with 156 receiving touchdowns, set the single-season record with 23 for New England in 2007, and earned a Hall of Fame place in 2018.The useful lesson is narrower than a slogan. A bad file is information, not a verdict. Teams that ask what surrounds a player, such as veteran leaders, a clear role and a steady coach, tend to decide better than teams that just count red flags. Minnesota did that homework. The Cowboys will face the Texans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Travis Etienne Jr. Injured, Latest News on Saints RB's Status, Timeline and Fantasy Implications
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints will be without their starting running back for several weeks.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints will be without their starting running back for several weeks.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Travis Etienne Jr. will be placed on the injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury, meaning he'll have to miss at least four games.

Etienne, who is in his first season with New Orleans, went to the locker room halfway through the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders and did not return.

After a career season with the Jacksonville Jaguars a year ago, Etienne has gotten off to a bit of a slow start, recording 128 rushing yards on 30 carries through the first three games.

Etienne's absence over the next few weeks means Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller should see an increase in touches for the time being. Kamara has rushed for 51 yards on 18 carries this year, while Miller has 44 yards on 13 carries. Neither running back has found the end zone yet.

For fantasy managers looking for a replacement for Etienne, Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon and New York Jets running back Braelon Allen jump out as possible candidates.

Dolphins' starting running back De'Von Achane landed on the injured reserve this week and Jaylen Wright is questionable heading into Week 4, so Gordon should get the bulk of the carries.

The Jets are likely to be without Breece Hall this week, and Allen is the first up behind him.

All things considered, the Saints have had a decent start to the year. After taking the Detroit Lions to overtime in Week 1, they upset the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2. They're coming off a one-score loss to the Raiders and have a manageable game against the Atlanta Falcons on deck.

Still, losing Etienne will make things a bit more difficult.

articles.title: "I guess I'm a little sick": Josh Allen opens up on his knee injury concerns ahead of Week 4 clash against the New England Patriots
articles.summary: Josh Allen, the Buffalo Bills’ star player, has always bounced back on the field in the last few years even as he sustained brutal injuries on the field.
articles.body: Josh Allen, the Buffalo Bills’ star player, has always bounced back on the field in the last few years even as he sustained brutal injuries on the field. Despite his record breaking performance in the last few seasons, the Buffalo Bills have missed out on winning the Super Bowl. While the team has recorded a winning streak in the new season so far, at the Week 3 clash against the Los Angeles Chargers, there have been some concerns about Josh Allen’s knee.Josh Allen reflects on his injury as he gears up to face the New England Patriots in Week 4A few hours ago, the 4 time Pro Bowler Josh Alen spoke to reporters about injury concerns as he said, "I guess I'm a little sick because I do love this game…”The Buffalo Bills’ top quarterback added, “I love everything about it. I do enjoy waking up on a Tuesday feeling extremely sore, especially after a win. It means that you did what you could do and found a way to win a football game. You're always going to feel more sore after the losses. But it does kind of put things in perspective…”Josh Allen also weighed in how the hits have now started to add up as he said, "Those sneaks aren't as glamorous as everyone thinks they are,...You're putting yourself up to getting some nice little hits on you there.”The top quarterback added, "And I know that to do this as well as I want to play and to play as long as I want to play, I know that I have to limit those hits," Allen continued. "And I haven't been doing a great job of that early on this season. So just finding ways to, again, take those hits off me and getting touchdowns to other guys."Buffalo Bills remains confident about Josh Allen even as he looked visibly in painWhile there have been many concerns about Josh Allen’s injury, the Buffalo Bills’ head coach Joe Brady seems relaxed about it.At a press conference, the Buffalo Bills’ head coach Joe Brady said, "I'd love for him to not take some of the hits. He's a competitor, and I have to take that into consideration with some play calling as well."For the unversed, Josh Allen led the Buffalo Bills to defeat the Los Angeles Chargers but ended up with a knee injury.Though Josh Allen continued to play, post match footage showed him visibly in pain as Josh Allen limped away from the field.However, the popular quarterback has remained regular at practice sessions as he gears up for the Week 4 clash against the New England Patriots amid a winning streak.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Injury Update, Latest News on Cowboys CB's Status After Steelers Trade
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who arrived in town after the Pittsburgh Steelers traded him on Wednesday, hopes he'll be able to make his debut Sunday at the Houston Texans as he continues to work his way onto the field from a back injury.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who arrived in town after the Pittsburgh Steelers traded him on Wednesday, hopes he'll be able to make his debut Sunday at the Houston Texans as he continues to work his way onto the field from a back injury .

"We're just trying to take things day by day, and if everything looks good, then we should be out there," Porter said following his first Cowboys practice on Thursday, per ESPN's Todd Archer .

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed optimism about Porter's chances, via Archer.

"We'd like him to play, but we'll see how the week goes. I think he's excited about the opportunity to maybe play, but we'll see how the rest of the week goes. But it was a good start today," Schottenheimer said.

Porter, a former Penn State star, was the No. 32 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. He played his first three seasons with the Steelers, amassing 165 tackles (120 solo), 31 pass breakups and three interceptions over 47 games (41 starts).

Last year, opposing quarterbacks only completed 32-of-66 passes in his direction en route to a paltry 57.2 QB rating, per Pro Football Reference .

Porter entered this season on the final year of his rookie contract, and he and the Steelers worked toward a contract extension. However, one never materialized, leading to a months-long standoff.

Archer and ESPN's Brooke Pryor provided more information on Porter, who did not participate in any offseason activities leading into the regular season.

"The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle."

Porter hasn't played in the Steelers' first three games as he deals with the aforementioned back issue plus conditioning concerns. He gave some insight to reporters (h/t Pryor) about the matter on Wednesday.

"It's both," Porter said. "My back has its moments where [there's] a flare-up here and there, and we're still just trying to get my conditioning down to just me being out there as much as possible."

The Steelers soon traded Porter to Dallas for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder. Now he'll joins a pass defense that can use his services. The Cowboys have allowed the sixth-most passing yards per attempt ( 7.2 ) in the NFL. They've also given up seven passing touchdowns and no interceptions thus far.

We'll soon find out if Porter makes his debut. Kickoff in Houston is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Hypes Joey Porter Jr.'s Trade to Cowboys from Steelers, CB Can 'Shut a Side Down'
articles.summary: Dak Prescott was excited about the Dallas Cowboys acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Dak Prescott was excited about the Dallas Cowboys acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night.

"He's a good corner," Prescott said Thursday, per ESPN's Todd Archer . "He's the guy that can play physical, play man to man and take a receiver away, shut a side down. And now to have that on our side, playmaker when the ball's in the air. I know he went and got one on me on almost a 50-50 ball that he didn't make it seem that way at all. And when you've got a guy like that with ball skills and hunger for the ball, you want him on your team. I'm so glad we have him."

The Steelers sent Porter to Dallas in exchange for a 2027 conditional sixth-round draft pick as well as a 2028 second-round pick. He needs to be on the Cowboys' gameday roster for two contests this year in order for the 2027 pick to go through.

Porter's change of scenery came after he was unsuccessful in his attempt to land a new contract from the Steelers heading into the 2026 season. He eventually missed Pittsburgh's first three games of the year while dealing with back issues .

The former second-round pick operated as key piece of the Steelers' secondary from 2023-25, starting in 41 of his 47 games played across that span.

Last season, Porter racked up 52 tackles and one interception to go along with one sack in 14 games. His 14 passes defended ranked No. 12 among all players.

Porter has found success against Prescott in the past, picking him off during a matchup between the Cowboys and Steelers in Week 5 of the 2024 season.

Dallas only sits at 1-2 to open its 2026 campaign, although Prescott has still been largely efficient in the pocket.

He's completed 69.5 percent of his throws for 730 yards and seven touchdowns compared to one interception. Prescott's 80.0 QBR ranks No. 5 among 30 qualified quarterbacks this season, via ESPN .

As the Cowboys look to put their slow start behind them, expectations are high for Porter.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers says there is "zero debate" about retiring, yet his final Thursday night game feels like unfinished business
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers will play the last scheduled Thursday night game of his career when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit the Cleveland Browns at 8:15 p.m.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers will play the last scheduled Thursday night game of his career when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit the Cleveland Browns at 8:15 p.m. ET on Amazon Prime. He sits one win short of tying Tom Brady's record of 14 Thursday wins by a quarterback. Both teams are 2-1. The Steelers beat Cincinnati 30-27 last week, and the Browns edged Carolina 21-18. Pittsburgh also arrives with an 0-9 mark in Thursday road games against AFC North opponents. Rodgers, 42, plans to retire after this 22nd season, so Cleveland is his final shot at matching Brady's number.Is Aaron Rodgers really retiring after the 2026 season?Everything he has said points to yes. Rodgers signed a one-year deal with Pittsburgh in May after more than four months of deliberating. Asked whether this would be his last season, he told reporters, “Yes, this is it.” When he returned to training camp on July 28, a reporter asked if he was weighing another year after this one. His answer was short. “No. Zero debate.”That certainty changes how Thursday reads. Rodgers turns 43 in December, and this is his last scheduled Thursday game. Brady's mark is 14, so a win ties it and nothing more. There is no later date to push past him. Rodgers has 46 touchdowns and seven interceptions on Thursdays. Against Cleveland, he has thrown 11 touchdowns without an interception in five games.He does not sound sentimental about the night itself. “I just suck it up for those three hours and then know you get a reward on the back end. I think it’s part of the game now because of the money that’s in it. I think I’m just excited about the weekend,” Rodgers said. If the Brady record matters to him, he is keeping it quiet.Can the Steelers beat the Browns on a short week?History says be careful. Pittsburgh has lost all nine Thursday road games against AFC North teams, and four of those came against Cleveland. The Browns won 24-19 in a snowstorm two years ago. The 2019 meeting is remembered for Myles Garrett ripping off Mason Rudolph's helmet and hitting him with it. Cleveland has also won seven straight Thursday games, tied for the fourth-longest streak in NFL history.Defensive tackle Cam Heyward does not see the short week as a one-sided problem. “But the great thing about it is they got to deal with the same problems we are. So it’s an even playing field,” he said.The Steelers have roster questions, though. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. went to Dallas late Wednesday for two draft picks after a contract impasse, and Jalen Ramsey is questionable with a broken wrist. Jaylen Warren should carry the load again after a career-high 176 total yards against Cincinnati, since Rico Dowdle is out with a toe injury.The line play may decide it. Browns tackles have allowed a 13.5% pressure rate, second highest in the league, and Tytus Howard's 17 pressures are tied for the most by a right tackle. TJ Watt has 17.5 sacks in 15 games against Cleveland. Deshaun Watson has lost all three starts against Pittsburgh and been sacked 18 times. Mike McCarthy is 11-5 on Thursday nights, and the Steelers are 2.5-point favorites.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Says Steelers 'Disrespected' Him in Contract Talks Before Cowboys Trade
articles.summary: Before being traded to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday, Joey Porter Jr. was engaged in contract talks with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Before being traded to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday, Joey Porter Jr. was engaged in contract talks with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

In his eyes, he was being "disrespected" by the Steelers.

"It was a hard process, a lot of ups and downs," Porter told reporters on Thursday. "Definitely felt disrespected. Definitely felt undervalued. But that's old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm on to new beginnings, new chapters."

With his new team, Porter already feels like he's being valued more than he was in Pittsburgh.

"It was the value. I didn't feel like it was really that over there," Porter told reporters . "[Dallas] is showing me that they value me more over here. That's really all I need to show what I can do."

Porter is currently in the final year of his rookie deal and has a base salary of $3.052 million this season. per Spotrac, he has a market value of $27.4 million per year, which would make him the fifth-highest-paid cornerback in the NFL.

While Porter feels more valued in Dallas, the Cowboys don't plan to sign him to an extension during the regular season, according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz .

The Steelers tried to extend Porter over the offseason but couldn't reach an agreement before the season started. General manager Omar Khan said in August that the team didn't plan to negotiate a deal during the regular season.

Porter has not yet played this season, but he's coming off a year in which he recorded 52 tackles, 14 passes defensed, a sack and an interception while playing 94 percent of the Steelers' defensive snaps.

He allowed the third-fewest yards per coverage snap last season, only behind Las Vegas' Erick Sokes and Denver's Pat Surtain II.

Dallas spent the offseason bolstering its defense, but the Cowboys have still allowed the third-most yards per game (387.0) and the eighth-most points per game (27.3) through the first three games.

Clearly, Dallas needs more on defense, and Porter will look to provide it.

The Cowboys take on the Houston Texans on Sunday, and ESPN's Adam Schefter noted that there's "a chance" Porter will be available.

articles.title: Watch Ja'Marr Chase's Funny Response to Question About Travis Hunter's Growth in NFL in Video
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wideout Ja'Marr Chase doesn't have many thoughts on the development of second-year cornerback Travis Hunter as he prepares to face the Jacksonville Jaguars this week.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wideout Ja'Marr Chase doesn't have many thoughts on the development of second-year cornerback Travis Hunter as he prepares to face the Jacksonville Jaguars this week.

Actually, scratch that—he has no thoughts on the matter:

Hunter, 23, has essentially converted to cornerback full time this season after splitting time at wide receiver last year (and only playing seven games due to injury). In three games he has nine tackles and an interception.

Chase will figure to see plenty of Hunter lined up in front of him this week in a battle of 2-1 teams. Perhaps after the game he'll have a few more thoughts on the matter.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. says he felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by Steelers, wants to finish his career with Cowboys
articles.summary: The fourth-year cornerback was traded to Dallas on Wednesday after missing all of training camp, the preseason and first three games of the season with a bac...
articles.body:
Following Wednesday's trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers to the Dallas Cowboys, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. said the back injury that sidelined him through all of training camp, the preseason and the first three games of the regular season is "feeling better."

The fourth-year pro was ruled out for the Steelers' Thursday night matchup versus the Cleveland Browns to open Week 4. Yet Porter could be available for the Cowboys on Sunday versus the Houston Texans after being acquired for a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder, according to ESPN .

"He moved around good today," Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after Thursday's practice, via The Athletic . "It was a good start today. It was a positive first day."

Porter was not listed on the Cowboys' injury report for Thursday.

That would be an impressive recovery for Porter, whose injury status many attributed to him holding out for a new contract from the Steelers. Taking the field promptly after being traded to the Cowboys does little to dispel that notion.

Porter himself lent credence to the skepticism with his remarks about his experience in Pittsburgh to reporters on Thursday, saying he didn't feel valued.

"Definitely felt disrespected, definitely felt undervalued," Porter said, via the Cowboys' official website . "But that's old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm onto new beginnings, new chapters. I'm a Cowboy, I'm in Dallas, so I'm happy about that."

He laughed when it was pointed out that his back felt fine in Dallas.

Porter and the Cowboys still need to work out a new contract, which was the basis of his issues with the Steelers. Reportedly, he is seeking a deal that pays him a $30 million average annual salary , which would put him among the top six cornerbacks in the NFL, according to Over the Cap .

However, Porter appears to be assured that a new deal will be coming. He made it clear that he wants to continue playing in Dallas.

"I'm down with it if they are," he said, via The Athletic's Jon Machota . "I want to finish my career here."

Last season Porter Jr. played in 14 games for Pittsburgh, totaling 52 tackles and 14 passes defended with one interception. The Steelers' 2023 second-round selection (No. 32 overall) out of Penn State has three career interceptions in 47 games during his three NFL seasons.

articles.title: Le'Veon Bell accuses Pittsburgh Steelers of racial bias in comparing treatment of Black and White draftees
articles.summary: Le'Veon Bell claims the Pittsburgh Steelers don't pay their black draft picks while paying white ones, but the facts tell a very different story.
articles.body: Le'Veon Bell is among the Pittsburgh Steelers most productive running backs of all time, joining a list that includes multiple Hall of Famers. But as an observer of how his former teams do business, Bell put himself in the Hall of Shame on Thursday. Bell, who played for the Steelers from 2013-17, saw his former team trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys overnight after a contract dispute and decided it was all about race. Because Porter is Black. No, seriously. JERRY JONES GOES ALL IN AS COWBOYS TRADE FOR STEELERS' JOEY PORTER JR IN HOPES OF SUPER BOWL PUSH "I wish Pittsburgh paid their black superstars they drafted just like they pay their white ones they draft," Bell posted on X on Thursday afternoon. " ... hate to see porter get traded .. I thought same thing with [George] pickens? TJ Watt is worth every penny tho, so let's not get it confused .. but something needs to change." Now, Bell has said some wild stuff in the past. But someone needs to jar Bell's memory and adjust his grasp of facts to get him off this race-baiting narrative. Bell, you see, is not an honest broker. He was drafted in the second round by the Steelers in 2013 and after three 1,000-yard-plus seasons, the Steelers tried to pay him. A lot. And that led to a contract dispute that ultimately ended his career in Pittsburgh. But before that happened, the Steelers offered to pay him $70 million on a five-year contract before the 2018 season. That offer from eight years ago, before the NFL salary cap jumped seven times, would be competitive with most running back contracts today. But Bell, who has admitted he came close to accepting the offer, ultimately turned it down based on his desire for greater guarantees. Those details aren't primary. What matters is that Bell lived through a negotiation where he, as a Black Steelers draft pick, was offered a lucrative contract by the Steelers. And still on Thursday he's saying the Steelers don't pay their Black draft picks like they do their White ones. The racist undertones of Bell's post also flies in the face of the fact that the Steelers, at the time of his offer, were coached by Mike Tomlin, who coached the team for 19 years until he stepped away this year. Mike Tomlin is Black. The team's general manager now is Omar Khan. He is a first-generation American of South Asian and Hispanic descent, with an Indian father and a Honduran mother. And those are the people who only want to pay White players? Pittsburgh's two-highest-paid players today are Watt and quarterback Aaron Rodgers. They are both White. But that has nothing to do with their pay because Watt is the team's best and most accomplished player and Rodgers is the quarterback who has earned the right to be highly-paid after winning four MVP awards ... and, did we mention he's the quarterback? But Pittsburgh's next seven highest-paid players are Black. And Pittsburgh's next nine of 10 highest-paid players are Black. The team has shown zero compunction about paying Black players. Receiver DK Metcalf got a big contract from the Steelers. He's Black. Defensive back Jalen Ramsey got a big contract extension from the Steelers. He's Black. Linebacker Patrick Queen got a big contract from the Steelers. He's Black. Receiver Michael Pittman has gotten two big contract extensions from the Steelers. He's Black. Someone challenged Bell about these facts beneath his post. And the former running back, who may be suffering from too many blows to the head, shot back that none of those players were drafted by the Steelers. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Except, running back Jaylen Warren got a big contract from the Steelers, as did defensive lineman Keeanu Benton, as did tight end Darnell Washington. All were drafted by the Steelers. All are Black. All got paid. And then there's defensive lineman Cam Heyward. He was drafted by the team in 2011, so he was there when Bell was on the team. The Steelers renegotiated Heyward's rookie deal, rewarding him with more money before that initial contract expired. Then they paid him again in 2015, 2020, 2024 and before this season. Cam Heyward is Black. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: DeVonta Smith Injured, Latest News on Eagles WR's Status vs. Rams Amid Hamstring Issue
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles might be without their top wide receiver this week.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles might be without their top wide receiver this week.

Per ESPN's Tim McManus, there isn't "much optimism" that DeVonta Smith will play against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday as he continues to deal with a hamstring injury.

Smith has had a strong start to the season, hauling in 19 catches for 235 yards and a touchdown. He had a 117-yard performance against the Tennessee Titans in Week 2 before recording 65 yards last week against the Chicago Bears.

Smith also missed practice last Thursday before ramping up to play against the Bears, but it appears his chances of doing that again this week are slim.

Being without Smith would severely limit the Eagles' offense, and tight end Dallas Goedert is also likely to miss Sunday's game because of an MCL sprain he suffered in Week 2. Despite missing last week, Goedert is the team's third-leading receiver with 81 yards and a pair of touchdowns.

Hollywood Brown is also questionable this week because of an ankle injury.

With multiple receivers seemingly set to miss the game against the Rams, Philadelphia will need Dontayvion Wicks to take on even more of the workload. The first-year Eagle has nine receptions for 179 yards and a touchdown so far.

Additionally, Philadelphia will need to look to rookie receiver Makai Lemon more often after his slow start to the season, as well as Zach Ertz in the backup tight end role.

The Eagles came into the season hoping to make a case as Super Bowl contenders, but they haven't looked the part so far. Philadelphia had shaky performances against the Commanders and Titans before being blown out by the Bears, who were without starting quarterback Caleb Williams.

The Eagles will face one of the NFL's top teams this week, and potentially being without Smith will make things even more difficult.

articles.title: Eli Manning Gets Blunt on J.J. McCarthy After Vikings-Giants Trade
articles.summary: Former Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy likely hopes this trade to the New York Giants sparks a fresh start and helps him prove he’s a starting NFL signal-...
articles.body:
Former Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy likely hopes this trade to the New York Giants sparks a fresh start and helps him prove he's a starting NFL signal-caller. In Minnesota, McCarthy had only a handful of starts, along with an injury history and rollercoaster play.Nonetheless, he's still only 23 years old, and perhaps the Giants can unlock the potential that made him a Top 10 pick, which is something the Vikings couldn't do and decided to cut ties by trading him for a 2027 fifth-round pick. With McCarthy in New York, former Giants QB Eli Manning shared his thoughts on the former first-round pick. McCarthy now has to prepare for his opportunity behind starting QB Jameis Winston, who has been shaky since taking over for Jaxson Dart after the starter's season-ending injury. "He's a young kid," Manning said during a Sept. 30 appearance on "The Colin Cowherd Podcast." "For whatever reason, it did not work in Minnesota. But the kid's 20-something, 21, 22 years old, and it's a lot thrown at you. So I think it's just a fresh start coming in this year. I don't think they're, I don't know the game plan, but I don't think he's expected to come in and, hey, you're going to start playing right away. "You got Jameis Winston, a veteran. Give him time. Hey, learn the system, be around, just relax a little bit, and who knows? Just kind of a restart and give this guy a chance. Maybe down the road, he could be a backup for a little bit, be a project and see what happens. He's had success and is a young kid, and I think there's a chance he can make this a turnaround opportunity."

Giants OC Matt Nagy on Former Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy

Meanwhile, Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy shared his early verdict on what he's seen from McCarthy since the trade on Sept. 28."He's done well since he's been here," Nagy told reporters on Oct. 1. "I didn't do a whole lot on him coming out, so I didn't know a whole lot about him, but I talked to a lot of people, got a lot of good reviews back from it, and I think that really the last 48 hours that he's been here, just like most guys, they're going to come in here and grind and then dig into it. "It's crazy because you're basically taking all of OTAs, just trying to learn the foundation, which guys have done in five or six months, and now taking that into two days. So he's done a great job with it. We're impressed. It's impressive. But at the same point in time, too, we also understand that it can be a lot. So there's a little bit of a balance."

Why Giants Decided to Trade for J.J. McCarthy

Furthermore, Amazon Prime's NFL insider, James Palmer, recently shared why New York opted to pursue McCarthy over other options to improve their depth after Dart's season-ending injury. "The other part is playing style," Palmer said in a Sept. 29 video on his X account. "That played a big part because Matt Nagy and that entire offensive staff spent the entire offseason coming into town with John Harbaugh and putting into place an offense that was designed around a quarterback who is mobile, a quarterback who can use his legs, a quarterback who can kind of throw on the move. "Those are things that Jaxson Dart was great at, and those are things that J.J. McCarthy can do as well. That's why you see oftentimes there are a lot of similarities in some buildings between the backup and the quarterback's strengths in this."

articles.title: Bills QB Josh Allen just made NFL history no player has before
articles.summary: Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills has officially reached a new milestone.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are sitting pretty at 3-0 to start the season, and quarterback Josh Allen has a good deal to do with that success. The MVP-winning quarterback is already clocking impressive numbers and making a statement as he tries to take this franchise all the way.

Now, Allen is getting respect in the NFL. Not that he didn't have it before, but it's continuing for the 2026-27 season.

In a piece for CBS Sports, Garrett Podell ranks each of the NFL's quarterbacks going into Week 4 . "A quarterback's resume and their performance throughout the season, not just week to week, are parts of the formula used by yours truly to concoct these rankings," he says.

Josh Allen remains among the NFL's top quarterbacks

He has Allen at No. 4 on this tally. While that's good, he's actually down three spots from last week because of turnovers.

"Josh Allen and the Bills' offense were stuck in the mud for much of the day in their 24-16 win over the now 0-3 Los Angeles Chargers ," he notes in the piece. "The team committed five turnovers with Allen responsible for three of them (two interceptions and a lost fumble)."

But, here's where the good stuff starts. Per Podell, Allen is the very first player in NFL history with five-plus passing touchdowns and five-plus rushing touchdowns through the first three games of a season. "That's good enough to remain in the top four," he says.

So, Allen has some things to work on. But, overall, the Bills' fanbase has nothing to complain about yet.

articles.title: Mike McDaniel Defends Justin Herbert, Takes Blame for Chargers Offensive Struggles
articles.summary: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season amid the Los Angeles Chargers' offensive struggles, but offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel isn't letting his quarterback take the fall.
articles.body:
Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season amid the Los Angeles Chargers' offensive struggles, but offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel isn't letting his quarterback take the fall.

"I'm fully responsible," he told reporters Thursday. "... I spend zero time trying to avoid blame. It's quite the opposite."

McDaniel, who was fired by the Miami Dolphins in January, hoped to use his offensive mind to make the Chargers Super Bowl candidates, but that hasn't been the case thus far.

Los Angeles ranks in the bottom half of the NFL in yards per game (349.3) and ranks fourth-to-last in points per game (14.7).

Herbert has thrown for 627 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions through three games.

Despite the Chargers' struggles, head coach Jim Harbaugh said this week that he has no plans to take some of the offensive control from McDaniel.

"No, we trust Mike. We believe in Mike," Harbaugh told reporters .

This week will be the biggest test so far as the Chargers go up against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, who have had one of the best defenses in the NFL early on.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns vs. Pittsburgh Steelers NFL Week 4 Live Updates, Highlights and Analysis
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are in uncharted waters—at least for them.
articles.body:
Three keys to a Cleveland victory in Week 4.

Don't Beat Yourself: It goes without saying that turnovers are the kiss of death. But the Browns are also the AFC's most-penalized team after three games. Todd Monken has to get that cleaned up.

Run the Damn Ball: The Browns are averaging just 87.7 yards per game on the ground—fourth-worst in the NFL. Quinshon Judkins is averaging three yards a carry. The Browns have to get the run game going.

Make Aaron Rodgers Uncomfortable: He may be old, but he's still Aaron Rodgers. Let him sit in a clean pocket and go through his reads, and he's going to find somebody open. The Browns need to heat Rodgers up and disrupt his rhythm.
